title: Pachca MCP tool manifest
description: The contract a consumer validates before it boots. The server keeps no list of its own: it loads this file and serves exactly what is here. One tool stands on one API operation, except for the few that absorb a chain step; what a token may see is decided by the audience listings.

schema_version.description: Major changes when a consumer has to be updated.

generated_from.description: A digest of the manifest content: everything in the file but this field, whichever input it came from — the spec, its translation, the rules or the prose. Equal digests mean equal manifests, and any change to what the manifest says changes the digest.

icons.description: Icons of the server, as the protocol's Implementation describes them: images that exist on the documentation site.

instructions.description: The always-on block a model reads before its first call: the catalogue of tools, who the caller is, today and the days after it, and the few rules a model needs before it loads a tool. Carries {placeholders} the server fills in every response that carries the instructions. One text, whole within 2048 characters with the placeholders filled — the most a widely used client keeps, and it drops the end silently, where the rule on honesty stands; the rules of one area live on the tools of that area. The build leaves room for a long name, and the server keeps the filled text within 2048 UTF-16 units all the same, shortening the name in {caller} when it has to.

instruction_placeholders.description: What each placeholder in the instructions stands for, ending with an example in «…». They belong to the caller, to the day and to the installation, so the server fills them in every response that carries the instructions (the result of initialize or of server/discover), from the token of that request: the date has to be known before the first call, and nothing else is in front of the model then. The caller carries the kind of token and, for a personal token, the role; today carries its UTC offset, and days the dates of the seven days after it. app_host is used by web_links rather than by the instructions.

cache.description: Listings and instructions are personal — what a token may see decides what comes back, and the instructions carry the caller and the day — so nothing here may be cached on a shared intermediary.

scope.description: The cacheScope every list result carries.

ttl_ms.description: The ttlMs every list result carries: how long a client may keep a listing of tools for one token before asking again.

discover.description: How the answer of server/discover, which carries the filled instructions, is cached.

response_format.description: How a tool answers: the rules live here rather than in the server, so results do not differ per handler. Most entries are one line of text, with a template in «…» where the server writes exact words; the shape of the text half is a list of lines. Which values of an answer are text of other people, each tool lists itself (tool.untrusted).

refusals.description: What an agent should do when a call is refused, by HTTP status. Every status from 400 up that an operation of a tool declares has a line, and every line answers such a status; a code a line names in backticks is a code of the spec.

compact_projections.description: The card of each entity that has one. A list or a search of such an entity cuts each record to its card unless view is full; a read of one record answers whole, apart from what single_read_omit names, and a write answers with the whole record. A name keeps that field. A dotted name keeps that part of a nested object, of every item where the object is a list; a field or a parent that is null or absent stays as it is, so thread.id keeps thread: null. The cut record still fits the tool's outputSchema.

single_read_omit.description: Fields a read of one record keeps out of its default answer, by entity: secrets that act as a bot, and the like. The argument whose effect is omission names the entity; view: full returns these fields too. Dotted names and null parents follow compact_projections. An entity named nowhere here is read whole.

authors.description: Who wrote a record, by entity, for response_format.own_items: the record whose author is the caller is marked «(you)». An entity named nowhere here has no author. The author is compared with the caller's id as text, since some ids are strings.

field.description: The field holding the author, a dotted name as in compact_projections.

prefer.description: A field that is the author instead whenever it holds a value: the author of the original of a forwarded message.

when.description: field names the author only in records where this other field has this value.

web_links.description: Links into the web app for an item the API answers without one, by kind: response_format.compat answers every item with a link. {app_host} is filled as in instruction_placeholders, the other placeholders from the record. A message carries url in the API, which is used as it is.

compat_address.description: Where the compatibility pair (service tools with compat: true) is served: the same server at its own address, the address of the main endpoint with path_suffix appended. A listing has to stay the same per connection and may differ only by authorization, and a client's description of itself is no ground for behaving differently; another address is another server, so a client that needs the pair is connected there.

path_suffix.description: Appended to the path of the main endpoint: /mcp becomes /mcp/compat.

serves.description: What a listing at that address holds.

authorization.description: How a token is checked at that address. A separate server URL is a separate protected resource with its own metadata, so this says which authorization server, scopes and tokens it shares with the main address.

files.description: Files crossing the server. A file argument takes its contents in base64 or a link, and the server downloads a link itself, so the limits on links are the server’s to keep. A file handed back to the model (response_format.binary_body) is held to what the strictest client takes, not to what the server can download.

url_schemes.description: The only schemes a link may use.

public_hosts_only.description: true: a link to a private, loopback or link-local address is refused, and so is one that redirects there.

max_redirects.description: How many redirects a download follows, each one checked like the link itself.

max_download_bytes.description: The largest file downloaded from a link a model passes.

max_return_bytes.description: The largest file handed back to the model as a blob resource, counted as its base64 text like max_image_bytes; a larger one is named, not passed.

max_image_bytes.description: The largest image handed back as an image block, counted as its base64 text: the smallest limit a client sets for one image.

service_tools.description: Tools that are not one API operation: the generic search and fetch pair one platform requires, which call several operations each and are served at compat_address.

audiences.description: What each kind of token receives at the main address. The protocol allows a different listing per authorization, and a tool a role is always refused — its scope never given to the role, or the operation itself closed to it (tool.roles) — is not shown at all. The compatibility pair is not listed here: compat_address says where it is served.

jsonSchema.description: A JSON Schema without composition keywords: several clients silently drop a tool whose schema carries $ref, allOf, oneOf, anyOf or not. This schema checks the root; the build checks every depth. The root is an object, as the protocol requires of a tool's arguments and of its structured answer. A format is a hint to the model: the server reads a value by its type (response_format.argument_reading).

additionalProperties.description: false on a tool's arguments; a schema where a value is a map — link previews by URL, errors by field.

annotations.description: What a client shows the person. Clients group tools by these and let one decision cover a group, so the flags decide what a single «always allow» opens.

title.description: What a client shows instead of the name: the title line of the operation in the spec.

operation.description: The one API operation this tool stands on.

scope.description: Read from x-requirements of the operation. Never written by hand, so a permission change in the spec cannot drift away from here. An operation the tool runs besides its own brings its scope to the argument that triggers it.

roles.description: Who the operation answers to: x-requirements.roles of the operation where it answers to fewer roles than its scope is given to, otherwise x-scope-roles of its scope. Never written by hand.

bot_token_only.description: Only a bot token reaches the operation: roles is bot alone.

outputSchema.description: The structured half of an answer: the response body as the API gives it, data and, for a list, meta — except for a file and a redirect, whose structured half response_format describes (binary_body, redirect). A list cuts each record to its compact card unless view is full, a single read keeps out what single_read_omit names, and a write answers with the whole record. Nothing in it is required, so all of them fit. It declares types and the null a field may be, and no enum, limit or format other than date-time: the values a field takes are in its description, and a value the API adds later is no reason for a client to refuse the answer.

entity.description: The entity a successful answer carries. A list or a search of an entity with a card in compact_projections takes a view argument whose effect is projection; a single read of an entity in single_read_omit takes one whose effect is omission. Any other answer is returned whole. own_items reads the author of the entity from authors.

untrusted.description: Paths of the structured half whose values other people wrote: the text half puts each such value inside response_format.untrusted_wrapper. A path names fields by dots; [] steps into every item of a list, {} into every value of a map, and a path ending at an object covers everything in it — data[].content, data[].files[].name, data[].details. Generated closed by default: every string without a closed set of values or a format, and every object of free keys, unless the rules declare that Pachca makes it (identifiers, cursors, links to Pachca, secrets, codes). The build fails on text of an answer that is in neither group.

request.description: How the arguments become the API request. They are flat for the model and the body is not, so every argument names its place.

headers.description: Headers the server sends with every call of the tool: a header the API allows only one value of is a choice already made, not an argument. Prefer: return=representation makes the answer carry the record the call made.

in.description: upload: the server uploads each file and puts the result at `at`; server: the server’s own argument, never sent to the API.

at.description: The dotted place in the body: message.content.

array.description: query, for a list: how it travels, read from x-query-array of the parameter. brackets: each value goes as its own name[]=value pair. Every list in the query carries it.

operations.description: upload: the operations the server runs to make each upload, in order — steps of the action rather than actions of their own.

scopes.description: upload: the scopes those operations need beyond the tool's own, read from the spec. Passing the argument without them is refused before the first step.

item.description: upload: what each item becomes once uploaded — file, the file object with its key and size filled in; key, the key alone, where the API takes a list of keys. An item gives its contents in base64 or a link the server downloads first (files), or the key of a file already in Pachca: an item that carries key goes as it is, without an upload, and an id is meaningful only beside a key.

effect.description: server: what the runtime does with an argument the API has no field for. Declared rather than known by name, so a new argument of this kind is a new version of the package and not a change in the backend.

entity.description: Cut each record of a list to the card of this entity unless the full view is asked for.
Keep the fields single_read_omit names for this entity out of the record unless the full view is asked for.

operation.description: Run this operation once the tool's own call succeeded.

at.description: The argument of that operation the value goes into.

scopes.description: The scopes that operation needs beyond the tool's own. Passing the argument without them is refused before the tool's own call, so the call never succeeds and leaves this operation undone.

into.description: The file argument the downloaded bytes fill: the server fetches the link under the files policy and sends the bytes as that field.

name.description: Prefixed like every tool, except a compatibility tool, which keeps the exact name its platform asks for.

compat.description: Served at compat_address only, and never in a listing of audiences: the generic search and fetch pair exists because one platform's research mode requires that exact shape.

operations.description: The API operations the tool calls.

scopes.description: The scopes of those operations, read from the spec. The tool calls an operation only where the token holds its scope.

outputSchema.description: The answer a platform prescribes, when it prescribes one: the compatibility pair answers in this shape (response_format.compat), and its descriptions say what id and url look like.

untrusted.description: As tool.untrusted, for the answer of the service tool.

model_tokens.description: Roughly what this listing costs a model if a client loads it whole. Clients that fetch a schema when it is needed pay a fraction of it.
